legend_html:
Alert level
red
orange
yellow
green
Levels are climatological shares of cell-days (red = top 1 %, orange 3 %, yellow 10 %).
Daily probability of a reported landslide per 250 m cell
1e-91e-81e-71e-61e-5
Calibrated probability at the alert cuts: yellow 6.4e-08, orange 3.1e-06, red 7.8e-06 (cuts are set on the prior-corrected score, so they shift a little by zone).
Log scale. A lower bound: only landslides that get reported count.
Susceptibility class (Stage 1)
very high
high
moderate
low
very low
Classes by area: very high = top 10 % of the state, high 10 to 20 %, moderate 20 to 40 %, low 40 to 70 %.
Priority
P1
P2
P3
Hazard alert x impact: red with high or very high impact = P1; red with medium or orange with high+ = P2; red with low, orange with medium or yellow with high+ = P3. Cells with nobody and nothing in a landslide's path are never a priority.
Impact class
very high
high
medium
low
People-equivalent a landslide starting in the cell could reach (homes, road users, facilities, pilgrims in yatra months, people cut off by a blocked lifeline road): low under 10, medium 10 to 100, high 100 to 1,000, very high 1,000 or more. Blank = none.
Lifeline roads
10,000 or more
1,000 to 10,000
100 to 1,000
under 100
People cut off or facing a long detour (to the nearest health facility, school or plains town) if this road is blocked; detours count by length, a full cut-off counts 1.
Long-term risk
top 1 %
1 to 5 %
5 to 10 %
10 to 20 %
Stage 1 susceptibility x year-round impact, by share of the state area. For planning; it does not depend on the day's rain.
